title: Compact-support perfectness
statement:
Fix the global finite-field datum [def-weil-finite-field-fiber] and the coefficient conventions [def-trf-coefficient-conventions], with $A=A_{E,n}=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$, $n\geq1$. Let $K\in D^b_{ctf}(X,A)$ [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude], where the structure morphism $a_X:X\to s=\operatorname{Spec}k$ is separated of finite type [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]. Then
$$
R\Gamma_c(X,K)\in D^b_{\mathrm{fin}}(A).
$$
Here compact-support cohomology is the ordinary coefficient complex $R\Gamma_c(X,K)=\operatorname{Fib}_s(Ra_{X!}K)$ of [def-trf-coefficient-conventions], with $Ra_{X!}$ as in [def-compact-support-direct-image-detailed], and $D^b_{\mathrm{fin}}(A)$ means the perfect category of [def-trf-categorical-trace]: objects isomorphic to bounded complexes of finitely generated projective $A$-modules, rather than all bounded finite-cohomology complexes.

For every geometric point $\bar x:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to X$ [def-weil-geometric-point] (so $\Omega$ is algebraically closed), its derived geometric stalk is also perfect:
$$
K_{\bar x}:=R\Gamma\bigl((\operatorname{Spec}\Omega)_{\mathrm{proet}},L\bar x^*K\bigr)\in D^b_{\mathrm{fin}}(A),
$$
with the ordinary-module interpretation of [pur9-def-derived-stalk].

note: *Recorded in advance* from chapter *The trace formula* of the source.

proof.text: Put $s=\operatorname{Spec}k$, $F=Ra_{X!}K$ and $C=\operatorname{Fib}_s(F)=R\Gamma_c(X,K)$ [def-trf-coefficient-conventions]. By [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude], $K$ is bounded constructible. Apply [prop-finite-compact-support-constructibility] with base field $k$, $f=a_X$ and coefficients $A$. Here $X$ is of finite type over $k$ by the hypothesis on $a_X$, $s$ is of finite type over $k$ by its identity structure morphism, $a_X$ is separated of finite type, and $\ell\ne p$ makes $\ell$ invertible in $k$. Thus all the field, scheme, morphism and coefficient hypotheses hold, so $F\in D^b_c(s,A)$. Clause (1) of [lem-weil-point-sections-finiteness] gives bounded finite cohomology for the ordinary module complex $C$. This is only a finiteness conclusion, not yet perfectness over $A$.

source.place: Paragraph 1: bounded constructible compact-support direct image and finite cohomology

proof.text: Put $\kappa=A_{E,1}=A/(\varpi_E)$ and $K_1=K\otimes_A^L\kappa$, with the derived change of rings of [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings]. Choose a K-flat representative of $K$ there. After forgetting the $\kappa$-action its tensor with $\kappa_X$ is the ordinary derived $A$-tensor $K\otimes_A^L\kappa_X$; this is the scalar-tensor identification [lem-pur-change-of-rings-tensor-comparison] applied termwise to that representative. The sheaf $\kappa_X[0]$ is bounded constructible as an $A$-complex: on the single stratum $X$ it is constant with finite module value, by [def-weil-finite-torsion-constructibility]. Thus [lem-pur-finite-tensor-constructible-cohomology] shows that every cohomology sheaf of the restricted $K_1$ is constructible. An interval $[a,b]$ of Tor amplitude for $K$ in [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude], tested on the degree-zero $A$-module sheaf $\kappa_X$, bounds its cohomology. Finally the same stratifications and trivializations are $\kappa$-linear: the $A$-action factors through the surjection $A\to\kappa$, so an $A$-linear trivialization commutes with every scalar of $\kappa$ by lifting that scalar to $A$. The finite module values killed by $\varpi_E$ are finite $\kappa$-modules. Hence $K_1\in D^b_c(X,\kappa)$.

source.place: Paragraph 3, first sentence: the bounded constructible residue-coefficient input

proof.text:
Apply [lem-fix-compact-support-coefficient-change] to $a_X$ and the reduction $A_{E,n}\to A_{E,1}$. The input $K$ is bounded constructible of finite Tor amplitude, as required, and $1\leq1\leq n$. It gives an isomorphism
$$F\otimes_A^L\kappa_s\xrightarrow{\sim}Ra_{X!,1}(K_1).$$
This is an isomorphism of $\kappa$-coefficient complexes on $s_{\mathrm{proet}}$. At this stage we have not interchanged ordinary module tensor and point sections.

source.place: Paragraph 2: coefficient comparison, before taking point sections

proof.text: By step 2, the residue input $K_1$ satisfies the bounded constructibility hypothesis of [prop-finite-compact-support-constructibility]. Apply that result at coefficient level $1$ to $a_X$. It gives a bounded constructible $\kappa$-complex $Ra_{X!,1}K_1$. Consequently step 3 makes $F\otimes_A^L\kappa_s$ cohomologically bounded, say in $[c,d]$. Since $F\in D^b_c(s,A)$ by step 1 and $\ell$ is invertible on $s$, [lem-sf-proetale-residue-tor-test] with $T=s$ gives Tor amplitude in $[c,d]$ for $F$ on the small pro-etale site. Thus $F\in D^b_{ctf}(s,A)$ by [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude]. This uses the pro-etale test, rather than applying the etale test to a pro-etale object.

source.place: Paragraph 3: bounded residue direct image implies finite Tor amplitude at the point

proof.text:
We identify the ordinary-module stalk convention with the geometric stalk used by the finite-free stalk lemma. Let $T$ be a $k$-scheme (so $\ell$ is invertible on $T$), let $M\in D^b_c(T_{\mathrm{proet}},A)$ be intrinsically bounded constructible, and let $ ar t:P=\operatorname{Spec}\Omega	o T$ be a geometric point. Write $
u_T,
u_P$ for comparison with the etale site. By [lem-sf-proetale-constructible-origin], choose a bounded constructible etale object $M_{\mathrm{et}}$ with $M\simeq
u_T^*M_{\mathrm{et}}$. For an etale module sheaf $G$, [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-pullback] gives $ ar t_{\mathrm{proet}}^*
u_T^*G\simeq
u_P^* ar t_{\mathrm{et}}^{-1}G$. Evaluating the unit isomorphism of [prop-weil-pbc-site-comparison-finite-level] on the final etale object $P$ identifies $\Gamma(P_{\mathrm{proet}},
u_P^*H)$ with $\Gamma(P_{\mathrm{et}},H)$ for every etale module sheaf $H$. By [lem-weil-pbc-geometric-point-pullback-stalk], the latter for $H= ar t^{-1}G$ is $G_{ ar t}$. By [lem-cbc-proetale-comparison-stalk], this is also $(
u_T^*G)_{ ar t}$, $A$-linearly. All identifications are natural in $G$, so applying them degreewise commutes with the differential of a representing complex for $M_{\mathrm{et}}$. The finite-coefficient module inverse image is exact by [prop-weil-pbc-proetale-constant-exact], comparison inverse image is exact by [prop-weil-pbc-site-comparison-finite-level], sections on $P_{\mathrm{proet}}$ are exact by [lem-weil-point-proetale-sections-exact], and the pro-etale geometric stalk is exact by [lem-cbc-proetale-classical-stalk]. Thus these termwise identifications preserve quasi-isomorphisms and give
$$R\Gamma(P_{\mathrm{proet}},L ar t^*M)\simeq M_{ ar t}^{\mathrm{geom}}\quad	ext{in }D(A).$$
Here the right side is the termwise geometric stalk and the left side is the convention [pur9-def-derived-stalk]. No equivalence between arbitrary pro-etale sheaves and ordinary modules is asserted.

source.place: Tags 09AL (lemma-compare-constructible-derived), 0GLZ (lemma-describe-pullback-from-etale); point interpretation supplied by the cited comparison and geometric-point lemmas

proof.text: Apply the finite-coefficient assertion of [fix-lem-finite-tor-perfect] to $Y=s$, $M=F$ and the identity geometric point $\bar s=\operatorname{id}_s$. Its bounded constructibility and finite Tor hypotheses are steps 1 and 4. It gives a bounded finite free $A$-complex representing the geometric stalk of $F$. Step 5 identifies this stalk with the ordinary derived stalk of [pur9-def-derived-stalk]; for the identity point this is $R\Gamma(s_{\mathrm{proet}},F)$. By [lem-weil-point-proetale-sections-exact] this is termwise $\Gamma(s,F)$, namely $\operatorname{Fib}_s(F)=C$ in [def-weil-finite-coefficient-point]. Thus $C$ has a bounded finite free model. A finite free module is finitely generated projective, being a direct summand of itself, so this model belongs to the perfect category [def-trf-categorical-trace]. This proves the compact-support assertion. The finite-free stalk lemma supplies the commutative-algebra passage only after step 4 has established finite Tor amplitude; bounded finite cohomology alone has not been used to infer perfectness.

source.place: Paragraph 3, last sentence: obtain the perfect ordinary coefficient complex at the point

proof.text: For any geometric point $\bar x$ of $X$, apply [fix-lem-finite-tor-perfect] directly with $Y=X$ and $M=K$. Its hypotheses are exactly $K\in D^b_{ctf}(X,A)$, and its finite-coefficient conclusion supplies a bounded complex of finite free $A$-modules for the geometric stalk. By step 5 this represents $K_{\bar x}=R\Gamma((\operatorname{Spec}\Omega)_{\mathrm{proet}},L\bar x^*K)$ in the ordinary-module convention [pur9-def-derived-stalk]. Hence $K_{\bar x}$ belongs to the perfect category [def-trf-categorical-trace]. The geometric point's source need not be of finite type over $k$: the stalk lemma quantifies over every geometric point, and step 5 uses only that $\Omega$ is algebraically closed.

proof_origin.place: Paragraphs 1-4, with explicit tensor-constructibility citation and the pro-etale residue test before taking ordinary coefficient fibres

split_report.summary: Seven steps and no new nodes. Audited finished-source candidates, added the existing tensor-constructibility lemma, tested residue boundedness before coefficient change, used the existing pro-etale residue test, and applied the existing stalk-perfectness theorem only after establishing the compact-support direct image is ctf. Made the ordinary-module meaning of the derived stalk and the perfect meaning of D^b_fin explicit. No full cohomological dimension assertion is used. Explicitly compared the geometric and derived-sections stalks via etale origin and the point comparison, without treating arbitrary pro-etale sheaves as modules.
split_report.blueprint: Realizes current blueprint proof paragraphs 1-4: step 1 gives bounded finite cohomology, steps 2-4 give residue boundedness and finite Tor amplitude, step 5 verifies the ordinary-module stalk interpretation, step 6 invokes the existing finite-free stalk/commutative-algebra result at the point, and step 7 gives geometric-stalk perfectness. The unit has no numbered steps and already lists this item in realized.statement.

tool_uses.why: Compact-support boundedness and constructibility used as a black box, preserving the unit route through finiteness and Tor amplitude.
Point sections finite-cohomology lemma, used for the first finiteness step; no theorem of this unit replaces that point identification.
Generic K-flat computation of coefficient extension, needed only to identify the residue complex.
Generic scalar/tensor identification on a K-flat representative, not a six-functor proof route.
Generic constructibility of tensor cohomology, filling the residue-input gap in the stated blueprint route.
Generic Artinian coefficient Tor test on the actual pro-etale site; replaces an ill-typed application of the etale-only test, with exactly the same residue route.
Exact point sections identify the derived coefficient fibre with the ordinary module complex.
Generic etale-origin theorem used only to compare the two ordinary-module stalk conventions; it does not replace the residue proof of compact-support Tor amplitude.
Canonical comparison of inverse images, used to identify the module-valued derived stalk for finite constructible inputs.
Exact comparison inverse image and its sheaf unit identify point sections of an etale-origin object; a generic comparison tool.
Point sections of an etale inverse image equal its geometric stalk; needed for the explicit typing of the ordinary-module stalk.
Generic equality of etale and pro-etale geometric stalks of a comparison pullback.
Generic finite-coefficient exactness of module inverse image, used to pass the natural stalk comparison to complexes.
Exactness of the pro-etale geometric stalk lets its termwise comparison descend to the derived category.
